meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so tell me who decided to put a zero in front of my son's whole class.

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. Now tell me what you're basing it on, and if the answer is a software score, we can both save time.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then show me. Turn the screen around.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.
I'm writing down those times. People paste from other places all the time, Hale, so that proves when it arrived, not who wrote it. Whatever happens next, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
Owen says he wrote it over the weekend. Did you ask him where, before you entered that zero?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.
Seventeen-year-olds change their minds in two weeks, Hale, that's what an outline is for. And you didn't answer me: did you talk to Owen before that zero went in?
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.
I'm searching it on my phone right now. Fine. What exactly are you proposing, Hale, and before you answer, anything that happens in front of his class or ends up on his file is a no.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
I didn't ask what it shows, I asked what you're proposing. You've got about twelve minutes.
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
A timed paragraph in class next to an essay he had weeks for, of course they don't look alike. I've seen your documents, Hale. Put an offer on the table or I'm taking this upstairs.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

To put this behind him, he'll do it, but privately, after school, not with his classmates watching. The rewrite mark replaces the zero, the zero comes off the gradebook today, and "nothing goes on file" comes to me in writing. Can you put that in an email tonight, yes or no?
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Lunch, alone with you. Okay. You still haven't said whether the zero comes off today and whether I get it in writing tonight.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

I've told you twice. An email tonight, cc your principal, saying the zero is withdrawn, the rewrite is private, its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. Do that and I don't go upstairs today.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Okay. Cc the principal, and give me a date for the rewrite well before December first, because his scholarship applications close then.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
Who marks the rewrite and against what, so it's the same standard as everyone else's essay. And I have five minutes, Hale.
Then I'll send it by eight.
Eight o'clock. If it isn't in my inbox by then, I'm in the principal's office at eight tomorrow morning.
Thank you for coming in.
We'll see what the email says. Tell Owen nothing until I've read it, I'll speak to him myself.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Not before I've read your email and spoken to him tonight. The date goes in writing, Hale, and Owen hears it from me first.
